867e0e751f578fc2: KUALA LUMPUR: Allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest could have serious implications for Malaysia's anti-corruption credibility, said Transparency International Malaysia (TI-M).

Its president, Dr Raymon Ram, said that while the organisation respected the constitutional power of clemency under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, Najib's conviction involving RM42mil had been unanimously upheld by the Federal Court.

"The concern goes beyond one individual. Exceptional treatment of a person convicted in a major corruption case risks reinforcing the perception that those with political influence or status may face different consequences from ordinary offenders.

"It may also set expectations for similar treatment in future cases involving grand corruption and financial crime, potentially weakening the deterrent effect of Malaysia's anti-corruption framework," he said in a statement.
He added that the case also had implications for Malaysia's international standing on the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) global ranking.
"High-profile decisions involving accountability for corruption inevitably contribute to the wider environment in which those perceptions are formed.
"Malaysia should be strengthening confidence in the integrity of its institutions, not creating further uncertainty over whether accountability is applied consistently.

"Malaysia's anti-corruption credibility will ultimately be judged by whether the principles of accountability, proportionality and equality before the law remain equally strong when those involved are powerful," he said.

Ram said the country's progress in strengthening governance and rebuilding institutional confidence must not be undermined by perceptions of preferential treatment in cases that have come to symbolise Malaysia's fight against grand corruption.

Earlier today, the Federal Territories Pardons Board said Najib had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed in the SRC International case.
The board said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.
It added that Najib must comply with all conditions imposed under the pardon, failing which the conditional pardon could be revoked.
52a26d674f2d90b3: MELAKA, Sept 19 — The Public Higher Education Institution (IPTA) Wi-Fi project, covering 539 locations nationwide, is expected to be fully completed by September, with 55 per cent, or 294 locations, already having access to Wi-Fi, Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said.

She said the RM664 million project, fully funded by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) through the Universal Service Provision initiative, would help upgrade infrastructure and improve internet coverage across campuses.
“We have embarked on a project to install tens of thousands of access points equipped with high-end Wi-Fi technology, specifically Wi-Fi 6 or Wi-Fi 7.

“This project focuses on strategic locations across campuses, including lecture halls, laboratories, libraries, student centres, residential colleges and hostels,” she told reporters after visiting the IPTA Wi-Fi Project Phase 3 site at Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) here today.
She said the project covers 539 locations, involving IPTA and skills training institutions under Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) and the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma).
Teo said Phases 1 and 2 of the project had been completed at 191 locations, with Phase 3 implementation now underway at institutions under Mara and Kesuma.
“For Phase 3 of the project, work has been completed at 42 of the 204 locations, or 21 per cent, while the remaining locations are still undergoing network provisioning and installation.

“As for institutions under Mara, work has been completed at 60 of the 110 identified locations, or 55 per cent, while for those under Kesuma, work has been completed at one of the 34 identified locations,” she said.

Commenting on the project’s implementation in Melaka, Teo said the IPTA Wi-Fi project in the state had reached 44 per cent completion, with 1,399 new access points activated at 10 IPTA as of last August.
She said UTeM had made good progress under Phase 3, with 302 additional access points installed on Aug 27, ahead of the MCMC’s original target date of Sept 23.
“Under Phase 3, 302 additional APs were installed here at UTeM, with the work completed on Aug 27, ahead of the MCMC’s original target date of Sept 23.
“In total, UTeM now has 410 operational APs, including the 108 APs installed under Phase 2 in June 2025,” she said.

Meanwhile, UTeM student representative Muhammad Quwayyis Khairuddin, 21, said the installation of additional high-speed Wi-Fi APs was crucial, particularly for students living in residential colleges and those using other strategic locations across the university campus.
“This is a meaningful contribution from the Ministry of Communications, as every student here needs reliable internet access to complete projects and assignments.
“Although the internet service was already good, the addition of these APs has further improved internet connectivity across the campus,” he said. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: IPTA stands for Institusi Pengajian Tinggi Awam, the Malay name for Public Higher Education Institutions.

d77b9a7ef56304b1: KUALA LUMPUR: Actress Elza Irdalynna recently shared a terrifying experience from the filming of the movie Anak Mami Kembali over two decades ago.

"We had to change the filming location because Saiful couldn't make it to the set on time. The original location was at a jetty, which ended up getting hit by severe flooding caused by the tsunami," Elza shared in a post on Threads.
Elza, who was working as her mother's personal assistant during the shoot, expressed how grateful everyone was for Saiful unwittingly saving their lives.
"He's our hero because his late arrival saved all of us," she said.
She recalled that a crew member later gave them a firsthand account of the destruction at the original set.

"He told us that boats at the site in Batu Ferringhi were smashed to pieces and scattered all over the road. We saw the full extent of the damage on the evening news later that night, and we were all in complete shock," she recalled.

e824eedc561f9a67: PUTRAJAYA: The Perdana Putra complex here came under close media attention today as the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council was set to meet amid heightened political developments surrounding Barisan Nasional's (BN) position in the unity government.

Several vehicles believed to be carrying political leaders were seen entering the complex from about 5.20pm, with members of the media gathering outside the Prime Minister's Office from about 4pm ahead of the scheduled 5.30pm meeting.
The meeting, chaired by PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, is expected to discuss current political developments, including BN's position in the unity government.
The identities of those in the vehicles could not immediately be confirmed.

The meeting comes amid renewed political attention following the decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under conditional house arrest, subject to a RM50 million fine.
Najib was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.

The decision has reignited political discussion within Umno, with analysts saying it could revive the "Bossku" sentiment among sections of the party's grassroots and increase pressure on Umno to be more vocal in defending its former president.

The PH meeting also follows remarks by BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi at the 2026 Umno general assembly last week, when he challenged those calling for the party to end its cooperation with the unity government.

Zahid said those seeking to end the cooperation should either call for the dissolution of Parliament to pave the way for the 16th general election (GE16), or table a motion of no confidence against the government in the Dewan Rakyat.
His remarks have since fuelled renewed discussion over BN's position in the unity government and the future of the coalition.
On Monday, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke called on Anwar to convene the PH Presidential Council meeting immediately to discuss recent political developments.

Loke said the meeting should be held as soon as Anwar returned from his official overseas visit, citing several political statements made recently which he described as detrimental to political certainty and stability in the country.
Today's meeting is expected to give PH leaders an opportunity to discuss the latest developments and their implications for the coalition's relationship with BN.
The issue is particularly sensitive as BN remains a key component of the unity government, while the Najib decision has generated strong reactions within Umno and among its supporters.
The media remained gathered outside Perdana Putra as vehicles continued to arrive ahead of the meeting.
As of press time, no political leaders had emerged to speak to the media.

b649159f7fb00b19: KOTA KINABALU: Nine policemen were discharged and acquitted by the Special Corruption Sessions Court here today of all charges of receiving bribes.

They are Inspector Joevian Gubal Michael, Sergeant Azizul Ismail, Lance Corporal Hairul Amid, Constable Afizul Azwan Anuar, Corporal Abdullah Bakir, Inspector Bobby Rhyne Warry Nawari, Corporal Haikal Ibrahim Abdullah, Corporal Sebestino Bong and Corporal Jameswell anak Lakin.
Sessions Court Judge Jason Juga made the ruling after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish the elements of the charges.

Jason said there were doubts in the evidence and that the prosecution had failed to prove the charges under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 based on a maximum evaluation of the prosecution's case.

"In evaluating the evidence presented before the court during the prosecution's case, based on the prevailing facts I found that there are doubts on the evidence forwarded which render the charges not proven that the Accused had obtained bribes under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009.
"On the strength of the prosecution's evidence, I'm not prepared to convict the accused in the event that they remain silent if defence is called.

"Hence, there is no prima facie case and therefore, all nine accused should be entitled for acquittal and discharge without calling to enter upon their defence under section 173(f)(ii) of the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC)," he said.
All nine accused claimed trial in 2021.
The nine policemen faced several charges involving different amounts of money, which they allegedly received from a man as an inducement not to take action against him for a drug offence.
The alleged offences were committed on various dates between April 2014 and July 2018, with the money allegedly deposited into the respective accounts of the accused.
Abdullah faced the highest number of charges, with 18 involving RM2,200, followed by Haikal with nine charges involving RM1,570 and Bobby with eight charges involving RM3,600.
Hairul faced five charges involving RM2,000, while Joevian, Afizul and Azizul faced four charges each involving RM2,400, RM470 and RM900 respectively.
Jameswell faced three charges involving RM600, while Sebestino faced two charges involving RM300.
All the charges were framed under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009.
During the joint trial, the prosecution called 24 witnesses to testify.
MACC prosecuting officer Dzulkarnain Rousan Hasbi appeared for the prosecution.

Joevian and Azizul were represented by lawyer Sylyester Kuan; Hairul, Afizul, Abdullah, Haikal and Jameswell by Mohd Azhier Farhan Arisin; Bobby by Batholomew Jingulam and Edward Paul; and Sebestino by Luke Ressa Balang.

92a03eb9d96f2e78: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Bursa Malaysia’s main index closed lower on Friday after a choppy session, while buying interest shifted to smaller-cap stocks, particularly technology and construction counters.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 9.18 points, or 0.54 per cent, to 1,665.56, from Thursday’s close of 1,674.74.
The benchmark index opened 1.98 points higher at 1,676.72 and moved between 1,661.79 and 1,677.83 throughout the session.
Market breadth, however, remained positive, with 625 gainers against 564 decliners. A total of 505 counters were unchanged, 1,172 were untraded, and 22 were suspended.
Turnover surged to 4.91 billion units worth RM4.87 billion, from 3.60 billion units valued at RM3.25 billion on Thursday.

Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said major Asian indices trended higher as lower oil prices eased US inflation concerns, while a tech-led rebound on Wall Street lifted sentiment.

On the domestic front, Thong said the local market could not escape broader foreign selling across emerging Asean markets, as a hawkish Federal Reserve, elevated US Treasury yields and a stronger greenback encouraged investors to favour US dollar assets.

“Nevertheless, local investors have shifted their attention towards smaller-cap stocks, particularly in the technology and construction sectors, resulting in stronger broader-market breadth despite the FBM KLCI’s weakness.

“From a technical perspective, the FBM KLCI has slipped to 1,665, while its relative strength index (RSI) at just above 30 indicates that the benchmark is approaching oversold territory,” he told Bernama.
Thong said this could attract bargain hunters, but with momentum still fragile, the index must first reclaim the 1,670-1,675 level to signal easing selling pressure.
Otherwise, the next support lies around 1,650-1,655, he said.

Heavyweight counters saw Maybank lose four sen to RM10.32, Public Bank ease three sen to RM4.77, CIMB fall six sen to RM7.63, Tenaga Nasional reduce 28 sen to RM13.04 and IHH Healthcare erase five sen to RM7.64.

Among the most active counters, Zetrix AI lost 4.5 sen to 20 sen, AirAsia rose 2.5 sen to 53 sen and FBSM shed four sen to 6.5 sen. Jaks Resources added 1.5 sen to 15.5 sen, while Top Glove slipped two sen to 77.5 sen.

Leading the gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries rose RM2.70 to RM42.80, Sunway Construction jumped 76 sen to RM7.88 and Time Dotcom gained 49 sen to RM6.41. Petronas Gas advanced 34 sen to RM17.50, while QL Resources gained 33 sen to RM4.19.
On the losing side, Petronas Dagangan shed RM1 to RM20.08, Nestle fell 94 sen to RM89.58, Hong Leong Bank lost 56 sen to RM22.54, PPB slipped 35 sen to RM9.36 and KLCCP Stapled fell 28 sen to RM8.31.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index fell 3.01 points to 12,411.72, while the FBM Top 100 Index lost 8.57 points to 12,210.37. The FBM ACE Index, however, advanced 48.15 points to 5,244.60.
The FBM Mid 70 Index jumped 236.78 points to 17,844.02, while the FBM Emas Shariah Index gained 38.12 points to 12,311.99.

Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.38 of a point to 185.24, while the Energy Index gained 5.48 points to 820.62. The Financial Services Index, however, fell 123.28 points to 19,412.63, while the Plantation Index shed 10.84 points to 9,496.44.

1e1927f32462592c: KUALA LUMPUR: The decision to allow Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest is charting new legal ground as the country currently has no specific framework governing home detention for convicted prisoners

Constitutional lawyer Andrew Khoo said neither the Federal Constitution nor the existing prison laws expressly provided a framework for home detention of prisoners serving ordinary criminal sentences.

He said although prisons came under federal jurisdiction and were governed by the Prisons Act, there were currently no specific rules regulating how a convicted prisoner should serve a sentence at home.
"As far as home detention and ankle monitoring are concerned, they are not yet part of our law for prisoners.
"There are provisions involving monitoring under anti-terrorism laws, but not under the ordinary criminal law framework," he said when contacted.
Khoo said the Prisons (Amendment) Bill 2026, which was tabled in Parliament in June, had sought to introduce changes to the prison system.
However, the bill has yet to be passed after the government deferred it and referred it to parliamentary special select committees for further scrutiny.
Khoo said the Pardons Board's decision involving Najib was therefore entering largely untested territory.
"When the Pardons Board specifies home detention for Datuk Seri Najib, in a sense they are charting new ground.
"Even under the proposed amendments, the home detention framework was not meant to cover the kind of sentence that Najib was given," he said.
He said the offences for which Najib was convicted and the prison sentence imposed on him did not appear to fall within the category contemplated under the proposed framework.
"That was meant for smaller or less serious offences.
"So this is now charting new ground," he said.
Khoo said the lack of an existing legal framework also raised practical questions over the terms of Najib's detention.
"There are no rules and no conditions that presently govern this.
"The announcement talks about terms and conditions, but these have not been specified.
"So there is a whole area of uncertainty.
"If you want to be a bit cheeky, can he have a jamuan? How many people can he meet? Can he meet people?" he said.
Khoo said the authorities would therefore have to formulate a specific set of rules governing Najib's house arrest.
"They have to create a framework of terms and conditions for him to comply with.
"Maybe they are drafting something now. But as it stands, there are no existing regulations on how someone is to be detained under home detention," he said.
He also questioned whether Section 3 of the Prisons Act, which deals with the declaration of prisons and places of imprisonment, could be stretched to accommodate home detention.
"Section 3 was not meant to cover home detention.
"It was not intended to create a hotel or a house as a place of detention," he said.
Khoo said the arrangement could also raise constitutional questions under Article 8 of the Federal Constitution, which guarantees equality before the law.
He said the Pardons Board was also bound by the Constitution in exercising its powers.
"The question is whether this amounts to special treatment. Are they creating an exception?
"It is something that has to be looked at, including whether it complies with Article 8 of the Federal Constitution," he said.
Official parliamentary records show that the Prisons (Amendment) Bill 2026 was given its first reading on June 23 before being referred to the relevant parliamentary select committees on June 25.

The government said during parliamentary proceedings that the proposed amendments were aimed, among others, at addressing prison overcrowding, strengthening prison governance and expanding rehabilitation programmes in the community.

88e1e8480b3cb6c5: PETALING JAYA: Two civil society organisations have raised concerns about accountability, equal treatment, and public confidence in Malaysia’s fight against corruption after former prime minister Najib Razak was granted a conditional pardon to serve the rest of his prison sentence under house arrest.

Transparency International Malaysia (TI-M) said while it respected the constitutional power of clemency under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, “exceptional treatment” could reinforce perceptions that politically influential individuals face different consequences from ordinary offenders.

"It may also set expectations for similar treatment in future cases involving grand corruption and financial crime, potentially weakening the deterrent effect of Malaysia's anti-corruption framework," its president, Raymon Ram, said.

Raymon said while no single decision determines a country’s score in Transparency International’s Corruption Perceptions Index, high-profile cases could affect the wider perceptions on which the index is based.
“The country has invested significant effort in strengthening governance and rebuilding institutional confidence.
"That progress must not be undermined by perceptions of preferential treatment in cases that have come to symbolise Malaysia’s fight against grand corruption,” he said in a statement.
Election watchdog Bersih said today's decision sent a "deeply confusing message" to the public, given the government's stated commitment to fighting corruption.

"On the one hand, we fight against corruption and abuse of power; on the other hand, those who are implicated and sentenced for corruption and abuse of power can be released," the group's steering committee said in a separate statement.

Bersih stressed that opposition to the decision should not be construed as disrespect towards the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, but said it was concerned that the decision would set a precedent for future pardons involving other convicted former leaders.
It said it would convene with civil society, youth and student groups to determine its next course of action.

a41cfe1577eabc55: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) is working towards opening the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) to the public as early as mid-December, with testing and commissioning by its Comprehensive Inspection Train (CIT) progressing well.

MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak said positive test results had given the company confidence to meet Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s challenge to open the rail service earlier than its original January 2027 target, during the school holidays.

The CIT, known as the “yellow doctors” due to its distinctive yellow stripes and role in detecting potential issues along the railway, began testing from Kuantan to Kota Bharu last month and has now entered its second phase from Kuantan to Gombak.

“We are now in the second phase from Kuantan to Gombak, and the test results have been positive. We accept the government’s challenge to open it in December, and our efforts are focused towards that target,” he told reporters during a CIT journey from Gombak to Kuantan Port City today.

Darwis said the Site Acceptance Test (SAT) had been completed, while the System Integration Test (SIT) was about 80 per cent complete. The step-up speed test from Kuantan to Kota Bharu also recorded positive results.
Testing will continue, with the train expected to complete full runs between Kota Bharu and Gombak by the end of this month, before proceeding with the Fault-Free Run (FFR) in October.

The special CIT journey involving members of the media from Gombak to Kuantan Port City took about 90 minutes, including passage through the 16.39-kilometre Genting Tunnel at an average speed of 160 km per hour.

Darwis said MRL was continuing to work with the Kelantan, Terengganu and Pahang state governments to facilitate the targeted opening, following the ECRL project’s 95.41 per cent completion as of August. Phase 1 had reached 97.65 per cent completion.
On fares, he said no decision had been made, adding that the rate would be announced by the Transport Ministry, with the government expected to ensure it remained reasonable.

Once operational, the ECRL is expected to cut travel time between Kota Bharu and Gombak to about four hours, compared with around seven hours by road. Phase 2, linking Gombak to Port Klang, is expected to be completed by December 2027, with operations scheduled to begin in January 2028.

Meanwhile, China Communications Construction Company ECRL Sdn Bhd (CCCECRL) project director and senior advisor Kong Qi said more than 40 CIT test runs and 12 freight train tests had been completed, with results so far showing positive progress.

He said the SIT, which began on Aug 21, covered 10 key areas, including tunnels, bridges, subgrade and tracks, traction power supply, communications, passenger service information systems, electromagnetic compatibility and integrated grounding.
“We test every curve and train stability. We found some parameters that needed adjustment, such as cornering, but they have been fixed. Up to now, everything is going smoothly,” he said.

Kong said the CIT had completed speed step-up testing of up to 176 km per hour on the first section, with tests on the remaining section continuing before moving to Automatic Train Protection (ATP) and signalling tests, followed by the FFR.

The CIT is equipped with specialised inspection systems that allow engineers to evaluate track conditions, train performance and railway systems under conditions that closely simulate actual operations.

Its inspection covers track engineering, traction power supply, signalling and communication systems. The train collects data on track geometry, rail profile, wheel-rail interaction, vehicle dynamics, pantograph and catenary performance, as well as signalling and telecommunications, enabling potential issues to be identified and rectified during testing and commissioning.

As part of the SIT, the CIT conducts real-time inspections and data collection along the ECRL alignment to assess the integration of key railway systems, including signalling, communications, traction power supply and the overhead contact line. — Bernama

ca95f399d7f62ba9: KPMG UK is laying off staff from the Tech and Data areas of its Advisory division and offering severance terms that one affected employee described as "insulting and disgraceful." The job cuts, affecting about 4 percent of the Advisory staff, were announced internally in July. Affected workers in the AI, Cyber, SAP, and Testing teams are scheduled to leave the consulting business next month. Insiders have now shared with The Register details of the payments offered to those set to depart. The proposed redundancy package, subject to consultation and the employee signing a settlement agreement, combines statutory redundancy pay with several enhancements. The document helpfully advises staff to divide their annual salary by 52 to calculate their weekly pay. The number of weeks to which each employee is entitled depends on their age during each full year of service: half a week's pay for each year worked while under 22, one week's pay for each year worked from age 22 to 40, and 1.5 weeks' pay for each year worked from age 41. "If you turned 41 while working at KPMG, the higher rate of 1.5 weeks' pay only applies to the full year of service completed after you turned 41," KPMG's missive states. "Redundancy pay is calculated based on the individual's number of years' service (up to a maximum of 20 years' service). If you've been at KPMG for more than 20 years, your most recent 20 years of service are considered when determining the number of weeks' pay you will be entitled to." KPMG's enhancements remove the statutory weekly pay cap of £751 and count partial years of service exceeding six months. Regardless of their length of service, staff are guaranteed either £1,250 plus statutory redundancy pay or eight weeks' pay inclusive of statutory redundancy pay, whichever is higher. The agreement also provides pay in lieu of notice, including employer pension contributions and, where applicable, a car allowance, according to the document. The document explaining the package includes an illustration of three employees alongside examples of the terms they could receive. Two of the illustrated employees appear delighted. The reaction among actual employees was less cheerful. One affected worker suspected that "protecting the profit pot for the equity partners is what is driving this re-org mostly." KPMG's UK partners received an average of £880,000 in the year to September 2025. "The payout scale is insulting and disgraceful," one affected employee told The Register. A KPMG spokesperson said: "As our market evolves, we are adapting where we are focusing and how we are set up to make sure we have the right skills in place to best serve our clients. To respond to these market dynamics combined with low levels of attrition, we are proposing reductions in some of our advisory client-facing teams and will support our colleagues throughout this process." The latest cuts come six months after KPMG eliminated 600 roles across its UK organization, including around 120 in Advisory. "The firm's consulting business has been under pressure for some time as market demand has remained subdued," said Duncan Aitchison, an analyst at TechMarketView, who estimated that the practice's revenue fell 9 percent between fiscal 2024 and 2025. "KPMG is not the only Big Four firm taking action to reshape its consulting business. In April 2026, PwC UK unveiled plans to bring together two of its three advisory businesses as part of a global effort to respond to the disruptions to the consulting industry caused by AI." ®

98f401c3e3cc9ca3: SEPTEMBER 18 — Women make effective political leaders by most of the standard measures political scientists use, including constituency service, cross-party cooperation and, in study after study, lower tolerance for corruption once in office. What they don’t get, almost anywhere, is a fair share of the seats.

Women held just 27.5 per cent of parliamentary seats worldwide as of the start of this year, according to the Inter-Parliamentary Union, a pace so slow that gender parity in the world’s legislatures is still roughly 75 years away. Malaysia sits below even that modest global average, not above it.

Women hold 13.5 per cent of seats in the Dewan Rakyat, short of the 30 per cent floor the country itself signed up to under the 1995 Beijing Declaration, and the country has never had a female prime minister or female menteri besar. Every major party has more distance to cover here than its convention speeches tend to admit, Umno included.

That’s not just an equity argument. Political culture itself gets better when more women hold seats. A study of more than 125 nations found that legislatures with more women see less corruption, even after accounting for a country’s wealth, culture and institutions.

It’s not that certain countries happen to elect women and also happen to be cleaner; the representation itself seems to matter. A separate analysis pooling hundreds of studies found something similar in governing style: more women in office tends to mean more collaboration and less of the score-settling that creeps in when women are scarce in the room.
None of this means any one woman is automatically better than any one man. It’s about what changes when a room stops being so lopsided, and what that looks like in practice.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A delegate holds up a placard reading ‘Puteri Malaysia Terbaik!’ during the Puteri Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur on September 10, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel

I saw a version of it firsthand, sitting in Dewan Tun Hussein Onn as an observer at this month’s Puteri Umno general assembly, watching a wing built entirely around women’s political advancement try to say how it actually plans to lead.

The wing’s chief, Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi, laid out a framework she called “Politik Kepercayaan”, or the politics of trust. Her point, once you strip away the applause lines, wasn’t complicated: trust isn’t something you ask for; it’s something you earn by showing up and doing what you said you’d do.
It doesn’t get built during campaign season. It gets built in the small stuff, long after anyone’s watching, like a party member following up on a complaint months after an election is over.

My first instinct, sitting through it, was to file the whole thing under assembly-season sloganeering. Every wing rolls out a tagline each year, and most of them are forgotten by the time the next morning’s papers come out.
This one might hold up differently, but only if Puteri Umno actually treats it as a standard rather than a headline. What makes it worth watching is what it’s responding to.

Umno’s credibility problem was never really about ideology. It was the space between what the party said it would do and what it actually did, a gap wide enough that senior Umno figures have themselves pointed to money politics and internal warlordism as the cause.
Measured against that specific failure, the “politics of trust” idea reads as a sharper answer than a typical convention speech usually offers.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi delivers her policy speech during the Puteri Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur on September 10, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Start with the refusal to over-promise. Nurul Amal was explicit that leaders should say plainly what the party can deliver now, what will take longer and what might not happen at all.

Giving up a rhetorical advantage like that is rare in politics. It also happens to be the one thing that still works with voters, younger ones especially, who’ve stopped expecting manifestos to survive contact with government.

Then there’s the claim that trust gets built between elections, not during them. Hasnor Hafiza Hussin’s version of it was almost anti-campaign: show up and follow through whether or not there’s a vote to win.
If Puteri Umno’s branches actually behave this way, checking in on complaints when nothing is on the ballot, that would be a real break from a culture that mostly shows up when it needs something.

The harder idea is about mistakes. The framework asks leaders to own their errors out loud, on the bet that admitting “we got that wrong” builds more credibility than managing the problem quietly away.
That’s easy to say in a hall full of supporters; it’s harder to keep up the first time it costs someone their seat.

Umno’s youth and grassroots wings haven’t traditionally been where its more deliberate voices sit; that’s usually been left to senior figures. But Puteri Umno, positioning itself as honest about its limits, treating criticism as information rather than attack and judging itself by what it delivers rather than how loudly it announces things, would be behaving differently from the factional norm.
That’s close to what “voice of reason” actually means here. It is not a policy position, just a refusal to fake it.

It also matches a pattern researchers find elsewhere. Honesty about limits, follow-through outside campaign season and owning mistakes instead of deflecting them are the same behaviours that show up in the research wherever more women hold office.
The overlap isn’t a coincidence but the framework working as designed.

A more practical argument sits underneath the rhetorical one, and it circles back to where this piece started. Grooming leaders before a seat opens up, which is what Puteri Umno called for, is slower than the usual scramble that follows a vacancy.

Given how thin the pipeline for women in Malaysian politics already is, a wing planning its bench years out isn’t just managing succession. It’s closing the exact gap the national numbers point to, one candidate at a time, instead of waiting for the party to notice it at nomination time.

None of this proves itself in a speech. It gets tested the first time an admitted mistake actually costs the party something, the first time the wing has to criticise its own side’s money politics instead of describing the problem in the abstract, and the first time a critic says something genuinely unwelcome instead of easy to applaud.
Malaysian politics has heard versions of this pledge before. Most didn’t survive past the news cycle that covered the announcement.

There’s a limit built into the structure, too. Puteri Umno is one wing inside a much larger party. However sincere its intent, it can’t fix a culture problem that runs well beyond its own membership, and it wouldn’t be the first framework to win good coverage at the assembly and quietly disappear before the next one.
Whether that happens is an open question. My read is that nobody in that hall, including the people giving the speeches, fully knows yet either.

What’s true is that the idea itself is better than simply asking people to believe, and Malaysian politics could use more of it. Puteri Umno now has to decide whether it’s willing to be held to its own standard once the cameras are gone.
* Rabi’ah Aminudin is an associate professor at the Department of Political Science and Madani Studies, International Islamic University Malaysia.

9d4a67cd2e44cc82: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's modern pentathletes Jacky Aw Jian Ting and Lim Pei Yao may have fallen short of reaching the final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, but national coach Nik Lini Hayati Nik Kazem believes the experience will be valuable for their development.
Jacky, 20, finished 17th in his semi-final group after accumulating 1,327 points across the five disciplines of fencing, obstacle, swimming and laser-run at the Anjo Sports Park.
Pei Yao, 16, had earlier finished 15th in her semi-final group with 801 points on Thursday.
"We have learnt from being here, experiencing the competition here," said Nik Lini.
She admitted the team's preparation had exposed areas for improvement, particularly in the laser run.
"Jacky's laser run used to be 10 minutes during the simulation we did, but he did 12 minutes here. We did some reflection on what went wrong.
"We didn't take into consideration the energy required for the events. After every discipline, there is a 15-minute break.
"When we did the simulation, they were stand-alone runs. This is on me."
Despite Jacky's 17th-place finish, Nik Lini said he achieved several of the targets set by the coaching team.
"Jacky is disappointed with the finish, but I feel he did well to reach our small targets," said Nik Lini.
"For example, he did 59 seconds in swimming when we targeted him to do one minute and one second only."
The coach also acknowledged that Malaysia still has ground to make up against the continent's leading modern pentathlon nations.
"We have to accept we are not competitive enough compared to other Asian counterparts, but our athletes Pei Yao and Jacky are still very young, at 16 and 20 years old respectively," said Nik Lini.
"They have a long way to go in the sport."
795878478b611990: KUALA LUMPUR: More than eight million domestic customers, or up to 90 per cent of Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) customer base, will benefit from the government's decision to raise the electricity bill protection threshold from 600 to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) a month.
TNB president and chief executive officer Datuk Shamsul Ahmad said the move would bring almost one million additional domestic customers under the protection.

"We understand that many people have been talking about increasing the protection threshold, and this is one of the positive steps taken by the government to provide greater protection for almost all domestic users," he said at a media briefing today.
On Sept 17, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the electricity bill protection threshold for domestic customers would be raised to 800kWh a month from 600kWh.
He said the move was an immediate measure to ease the burden on households facing higher electricity bills.
Under the measure, domestic customers consuming up to 800kWh a month will be exempt from the automatic fuel cost adjustment (AFA) charge, eight per cent sales and service and retail charges.
The additional protection applies to electricity consumption from Sept to Dec 31, 2026, with savings for September consumption to be credited directly to consumers' October electricity bills.
Shamsul said the increase in the protection threshold was aimed at reducing the impact of electricity consumption on consumers' cost of living.
He said the measure ensures consumers remain protected from changes in AFA rates, which are influenced by volatility in global fuel costs amid the crisis in the Middle East.
"It also takes into account the increase in electricity consumption due to the hot weather and haze currently affecting the country.
"As the national utility company, TNB's priority is to ensure that the people continue to enjoy a safe and reliable electricity supply," he said.

With the higher protection threshold, domestic users who use up to 800kWh of electricity could enjoy a saving of up to RM47 in one month, compared with the previously lower threshold of 600kWh per month, according to TNB.
Shamsul said TNB will bear an additional cost of between RM120 million and RM150 million from September to December 2026 due to foregone AFA surcharges.
He said the cost could potentially be higher, although current forecasts indicated that it was unlikely to exceed the RM150 million estimate.
He said that if the price rises beyond that level, the company would absorb the additional cost, even if it exceeds RM150 million.
"We made a commitment, we honour our commitment," he said briefly.
Meanwhile, Shamsul said TNB would discuss with the government the approach to be taken after December, including how the protection mechanism could be continued.

"We will discuss with the government what happens after December, including what the methodology or best approach should be, how we can continue to provide relief and manage the impact of the geopolitical situation in the world, which will have an impact on our cost of living," he said.
d932e97eb3a768fc: KUALA LUMPUR: Batu Kawan Bhd is selling Chemical Company of Malaysia Bhd (CCM) to TMK Chemical Bhd for RM939.87 million, while getting a larger stake in the enlarged chemicals group.
The proposed disposal is expected to give Batu Kawan a pro forma gain of RM598.16 million, according to its filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
Batu Kawan and its unit Eternal Edge Sdn Bhd entered into a conditional share sale and purchase agreement with TMK on Sept 18 for the disposal.
The transaction comprises RM438.55 million in cash and 262.5 million new TMK shares priced at RM1.91 each.
The new shares will give Batu Kawan a 20.8 per cent stake in TMK's enlarged share capital.
Batu Kawan plans to use RM436.55 million of the cash proceeds to repay bank borrowings.
Following completion, Batu Kawan and parties acting in concert will hold a combined 57.4 per cent stake in TMK, up from 46.2 per cent currently.
Batu Kawan said it would seek an exemption from the Securities Commission from making a mandatory general offer for the remaining TMK shares, as it does not intend to pursue one.
The transaction will consolidate CCM Group under TMK, creating a larger chemicals platform, while allowing Batu Kawan to retain exposure through its increased TMK stake.
Batu Kawan said the restructuring would enable synergies within the enlarged TMK group and strengthen its operational capabilities and market reach.
Batu Kawan shares closed 22 sen, or 1.08 per cent, higher at RM20.50 on Friday, giving the company a market capitalisation of about RM8.19 billion.
ed801410f7eb3c9c: CARACAS: The Venezuelan government and the opposition are close to an agreement to transfer the central bank's gold reserves, worth about US$4 billion, to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York from the Bank of England (BoE), the Financial Times reported on Friday.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report, which cited four people familiar with the discussion.
Under the proposed deal, the interim government of Delcy Rodriguez would gain legal control of the gold but would be unable to sell the holdings immediately, the report said.
Instead, the reserve could be used as collateral for government borrowings, including for reconstruction following June’s twin earthquakes, the newspaper added.
A spokesman for the British foreign office said the government was "not a party in the legal case to determine who should have control of Venezuelan gold held in the Bank of England".
UK Courts and the Bank of England are independent of government, the spokesperson added.
In response to a Reuters' query, the Bank of England said it is not in a position to act until there is a further order from the UK Court on who has legal authority over the account.
"This requires the parties involved in the case to approach the UK Court to settle the dispute," the BoE said.
Gold could be used to try to counter inflation
The Federal Reserve Bank of New York did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment outside regular business hours.
The Venezuelan government and the opposition could not be reached for comment.

Last month, Venezuela's National Assembly chief Jorge Rodriguez said the country was working on recovering gold ​reserves held in the Bank ‌of England's underground vaults, in an effort to counter surging inflation.
The Bank of England has withheld about 31 metric tonnes of Venezuelan gold for years, citing its non-recognition of the legitimacy of then-president Nicolas Maduro's government.

The BoE's refusal to release the gold goes back to early 2019 when the British government joined dozens of nations in backing then Venezuelan opposition leader Juan Guaido on the basis that Maduro's election win the previous year had been rigged.

The bullion has since been the subject of a prolonged legal dispute in British courts, and has not been released despite Maduro's capture by the US in January and a ​request by acting president Delcy Rodriguez to King Charles.

“The UK maintains its longstanding position of support for a democratic transition of power in Venezuela which reflects the will of the Venezuelan people,” the spokesman for the British foreign office said.
da5e2be8e28a35f6: KUALA LUMPUR: Angkatan Belia Islam Malaysia (Abim) menggesa pihak penganjur dan mereka yang terlibat dalam sebuah pementasan teater yang tular kerana didakwa memperlekehkan Rukun Negara supaya memberikan penjelasan dan memohon maaf secara terbuka.

Presiden Abim Ahmad Fahmi Mohd Samsudin berkata, pementasan teater itu tidak seharusnya dianggap sebagai keberanian berkarya, sebaliknya mencerminkan kecuaian moral yang boleh merendahkan asas kehidupan bersama kalangan rakyat Malaysia.

"Rukun Negara bukan slogan kosong atau bahan lawak pentas. Rukun Negara merupakan ikrar kewarganegaraan yang dibentuk daripada pengalaman getir negara bagi memelihara kesatuan, keluhuran Perlembagaan, kedaulatan undang-undang serta kesopanan dalam masyarakat majmuk," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Beliau berkata, Abim sentiasa menghormati kebebasan seni namun kebebasan berkarya bukan bermakna seseorang bebas daripada tanggungjawab.
“Terdapat perbezaan antara mengkritik kegagalan kita menghayati Rukun Negara dengan menjadikan Rukun Negara itu sendiri bahan penghinaan," katanya.

“Pihak penganjur dan mereka yang terlibat mesti tampil memberikan penjelasan, memohon maaf secara terbuka serta bertanggungjawab terhadap pementasan tersebut. Pihak berkuasa pula perlu menyiasat perkara ini secara tegas, adil dan berasaskan undang-undang."

Ahmad Fahmi berkata, ketika negara berdepan polarisasi dan kemerosotan kepercayaan antara masyarakat, pentas seni seharusnya mencerdaskan pemikiran dan menyemai nilai kemanusiaan, bukannya menghakis asas yang menyatukan rakyat.
ac698666cb5a14b9: KUALA LUMPUR: A 16-year-old boy with alleged links to a secret society pleaded guilty at the magistrates' court to voluntarily causing hurt to two victims with an iron rod earlier this month.
The boy, who cannot be named as he is a minor, committed the offence against the victims, aged 16 and 19, at about 10.15pm on Sept 1 in front of a housing area in Lorong Ikan Emas, Cheras.
The charge, under Section 324 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine, whipping or any two of the punishments upon conviction.
The boy entered his plea before magistrate Atiqah Mohamed @ Mohamad Saim.
The court fixed Oct 22 for sentencing, pending the completion of a probation report by the Welfare Department.
Deputy public prosecutor Amritpreet Kaur Randhawa urged the court to set bail at RM3,000 with one local surety and order the boy not to interfere with prosecution witnesses.
However, a lawyer from the National Legal Aid Foundation sought leniency, saying the boy worked with a lion dance association and earned RM1,500 a month.
The lawyer also assured the court that the boy's family would ensure his attendance at future proceedings.
The magistrate granted bail of RM1,000 with one local surety and ordered the boy not to harass any prosecution witnesses until the disposal of the case.
Police investigations found that the two victims had allegedly been assaulted by a group of seven men armed with weapons, including knives, pipes and a table leg.
On Sept 2, the Cheras district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department arrested three men in connection with the incident.
Police also seized an iron rod measuring about 57cm long.
d9f5e18489dd39ec: KUALA LUMPUR: Eco World Development Group Bhd has secured a prime residential site for S$208.1 million (approximately RM667.6 million) through a tender bid managed by the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA).

The acquisition involves a 4,283.4 sq m parcel located at Lorong Puntong / Sin Ming Avenue within the established Bishan planning area. The land award was granted to EcoWorld's wholly-owned subsidiary, Eco World Development (S) Pte Ltd (EWPL).

Awarded on a 99-year lease, the site allows for residential condominiums or flats with a maximum permissible gross floor area (GFA) of 11,994 sq m. According to Eco World's exchange filing, the tender price translates to approximately S$1,612 per square foot of GFA.

"We are delighted to be able to make our debut as a property developer in Singapore at such a prime residential location," said Datuk Seri Chang Khim Wah, president and chief executive officer of EcoWorld.
Chang noted that the project is slated for launch in 2028, and expected to be completed in the third quarter of 2031.

The acquisition aligns with EcoWorld's strategy to expand its development pipeline and geographically diversify its earnings base. While this is the company's first development on the island, EcoWorld has maintained a marketing presence in Singapore since 2015.
Management expects the new project to resonate well with Singaporean buyers, many of whom are already familiar with the brand through EcoWorld's townships and business parks in Iskandar Malaysia.

The RM667.6 million tender price will be satisfied entirely in cash, funded through a combination of bank borrowings and internal funds. A deposit of S$10.75 million has already been paid, with the next payment of S$41.27 million due by Oct 15, and the remaining balance due by Dec 16.

The site boasts strong connectivity and proximity to key amenities, which EcoWorld anticipates will appeal strongly to affluent upgraders and multi-generational families. The future development sits just 170 metres—a roughly 3-minute walk—from the Bright Hill MRT station, which is set to become an interchange station for the Cross Island Line by 2030.

Additionally, the plot is situated opposite Ai Tong Primary School and is within a two-kilometre radius of several major retail and nature destinations, including Thomson Plaza, Junction 8, MacRitchie Reservoir, and Windsor Nature Park.

While the gross development value and precise project costs have yet to be finalised, the board believes the venture is in the best interests of the company and expects the development to contribute positively to the future earnings and net assets of the group.
03ccde65a6d83f68: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The increase in coal prices to US$148 per tonne on September 10, 2026 will directly impact the cost of electricity generation, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir today.

He said coal prices showed a more moderate increase in August to US$130.67 per tonne from US$129.63 per tonne in July, while peak daily electricity demand reached 21,949 megawatts on September 9, which was 4.7 per cent higher than the August average.
Akmal Nasrullah added that the increase was still within the reserve margin range that the existing electricity supply system could accommodate.

“The government will continue to ensure that the generation capacity and electricity supply system are sufficient to support economic activities, meet the needs of the people and strengthen the resilience of the country’s energy system,” he said during a briefing on the global energy crisis on TV1 today.

Apart from coal, the price of crude oil and liquefied natural gas also experienced an increase with the average price of Brent crude oil in August increasing 8.9 per cent to US$90.88 per barrel compared to US$83.42 per barrel in July.
Akmal Nasrullah said the daily price of Brent also soared above US$120 per barrel this week compared to a lower average in August.

In addition, the average price of liquefied natural gas rose 13.2 per cent from US$19.32 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) in July to US$21.87 in August and as of mid-September, LNG prices were approaching US$30 per MMBtu.
Akmal Nasrullah said geopolitical and supply route disruptions could still trigger price spikes in the short term even as the global market adjusts.

“In this situation, the government will continue to ensure fuel supply security until December 2026 through three approaches, namely diversifying import sources, optimising domestic fuel production and strengthening long-term supply agreements,” he added.

According to him, the strategy of diversifying supply sources continues to be strengthened by sourcing crude oil and petroleum products from various regions, including the Americas, as well as exploring alternative sources from the African continent.
Akmal Nasrullah said this move is aimed at reducing dependence on any one country or supply route, especially as energy trade flows from West Asia continue to face uncertainty.

Malaysia and Thailand also strengthened energy cooperation through the signing of a production sharing contract and gas sales agreement for Block A-18-01 in the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area to open up space for investment, maintain production and ensure long-term value for both countries.

He added that international markets have been adjusting since March 2026 through inventory adjustments, optimising supply sources and redirecting trade routes to reduce the impact of disruptions to raw materials and production inputs.

“The government’s priority is to ensure that the domestic supply chain continues to function, the supply of basic necessities must be sufficient and global cost pressures do not excessively affect the well-being of the people and the continuity of economic activities,” he added.

Meanwhile, Akmal Nasrullah said job losses increased to 68,177 workers for the period from January to September 16, an increase of 15,196 workers compared to the same period in 2025 involving the manufacturing and wholesale and retail trade sectors.
He added that Socso has implemented job relocation for 143,653 workers for the period from January to September 11 through the Employment Insurance System and the MYFutureJobs portal. — Bernama
c71cce193c62fa30: JOHOR BARU: Johor Umno welcomed the decision to allow former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under house detention.
State Umno chairman Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the conditional house detention did not amount to a release or cancellation of his conviction.
He said the decision should be understood according to the law and terms of the official order.
"Datuk Seri Najib is still serving the remainder of his sentence as stipulated," he said in a statement today.

2aeb14a0bfa27f1f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) said today it will provide RM120 million to RM150 million in support as more households qualify for the expanded electricity tariff fuel‑surcharge exemption until the end of the year.

The exemption covers the automatic fuel adjustment, the RM10 monthly retail charge and sales‑and‑services tax, with estimated savings of RM150 million for eligible households, business newspaper The Edge reported today.
TNB said more households have been consuming higher amounts of electricity in recent months.
The government announced yesterday that households using up to 800 kilowatt‑hours a month will now be exempt from the surcharge, compared with the previous 600 kilowatt‑hour threshold.
The Energy Commission had warned in April that rising coal and natural‑gas prices following the Middle East conflict would trigger the surcharge.
The proportion of households paying the three additional billing components rose to 20 per cent in July from 13 per cent in January under the earlier threshold.
TNB said warmer weather, work‑from‑home arrangements linked to the Iran oil price shock and increased electricity use during the 2026 World Cup contributed to higher consumption.
The utility said raising the threshold will protect 90 per cent of residential customers from the extra charges.
A consumer using 700 kilowatt‑hours a month will pay RM40 less under the latest measure.
8b00010273100ed0: PETALING JAYA: Pengampunan bersyarat yang diberikan kepada bekas perdana menteri, Najib Razak, bukan keputusan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim atau Pakatan Harapan (PH), tegas Wanita PKR.
Ketuanya Fadhlina Sidek mengingatkan bahawa pengampunan adalah wewenang Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

"Jangan kerana perbezaan politik, kita mengaburkan kedudukan Perlembagaan atau menggambarkan keputusan ini seolah-olah keputusan perdana menteri atau PH," katanya di Facebook.
Terdahulu, Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan (LPWP) membenarkan Najib menjalani baki hukuman penjara di bawah tahanan rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028 menerusi pengampunan bersyarat.
Keputusan itu tertakluk kepada pembayaran denda RM50 juta serta pematuhan terhadap syarat ditetapkan.
Perkembangan ini mendorong pemimpin Parti Bersama Malaysia, Rafizi Ramli, menggesa Anwar dan kepimpinan PH mendedahkan semua syarat yang dikenakan terhadap tahanan rumah Najib.
Fadhlina berkata pengampunan bersyarat Najib sudah tentu mengundang pelbagai reaksi, mengambil maklum kekecewaan dan kemarahan sesetengah pihak.

"Kerajaan tetap mempunyai tanggungjawab untuk memberikan penjelasan kepada rakyat," katanya.
Najib kini menjalani hukuman penjara enam tahun yang telah dikurangkan daripada hukuman asal 12 tahun dalam kes SRC International.

Anwar dilaporkan berkata pengampunan hukuman Najib tidak menjejaskan prinsip kerajaan untuk terus mengambil tindakan tegas terhadap semua kes rasuah dan salah guna kuasa.
4ec7216fc2885707: PETALING JAYA: Umno hopes the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Najib Razak will give the party momentum ahead of the Melaka state election, says its president, Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Zahid said the development could have a positive impact on Umno as it navigates the current political landscape.
“I hope this will add value (to Umno) in the country’s current political landscape, insya-Allah,” Bernama quoted him as saying at a press conference in Jakarta, Indonesia, today.

Najib was granted a conditional pardon today allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of his RM50 million fine.

The legal affairs division of the Prime Minister’s Department said the conditional pardon was granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, following the 64th meeting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board today.
Elaborating on the upcoming Melaka election, Zahid said he had given Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman Ab Rauf Yusoh the mandate to hold discussions with any political coalition.
He said Melaka BN would submit its list of candidates for consideration based on feedback from various quarters, with assemblymen who had performed well to be retained where possible.
“We adhere to the principle of having ‘winnable, acceptable and likeable’ candidates who will aid the blue wave currently sweeping across the country,” he said.
eef7200c13ac3f4d: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Islamic Youth Movement (Abim) has called on the organisers and those involved in a viral theatre play allegedly mocking the Rukun Negara to issue a public clarification and apology.

Abim president Ahmad Fahmi Mohd Samsudin said the performance should not be viewed as artistic boldness, but as a moral lapse that risked undermining the foundations of peaceful coexistence among Malaysians.

"The Rukun Negara is not an empty slogan or a stage joke. It is a pledge of citizenship forged from the country's painful past experiences to preserve unity, the supremacy of the Constitution, the rule of law, and courtesy in a pluralistic society," he said in a statement today.
Ahmad Fahmi said while Abim respected artistic freedom, creative expression did not imply freedom from responsibility.
"There is a difference between criticising our failure to embody the Rukun Negara and making the Rukun Negara itself an object of insult.
"The authorities must also investigate this firmly, fairly, and in accordance with the law," he said.

He said that at a time when the nation faced polarisation and eroding trust among communities, the arts should enlighten minds and instill human values, rather than erode the foundations that unite the people.
7678c2915f3fc013: LONDON: Trent Alexander-Arnold was recalled to the England squad on Friday as manager Thomas Tuchel named his first selection since the World Cup.
England begin their Nations League campaign against world champions Spain at Wembley on Sept 26, the first of four matches they will play during the international break.
Real Madrid's Alexander-Arnold had not featured for England since June 2025 and returns after more than a year out of the international set-up, with Tuchel favouring other options at right back.

Brighton goalkeeper Jason Steele and Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott were also included in the squad and could make their England debuts. Scott trained with England before the World Cup but did not play in their warm-up friendlies.

Tuchel made 10 changes from the 26-man squad that travelled to the US, Canada and Mexico. Cole Palmer and Lewis Hall return alongside Alexander-Arnold, while the experienced pair Jordan Henderson and John Stones miss out.
Arsenal winger Noni Madueke was left out, with Tuchel selecting Liverpool's 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha, who will hope to earn his second England cap after making his debut in June against New Zealand.
After hosting Spain, England visit the Czech Republic and Croatia before playing the Czechs again at home. The remaining two fixtures of the group will be completed in November.
6103b19019889a43: KUALA LUMPUR: Singer Shila Amzah has admitted that leaving her family behind to build her career in the Chinese music market is never easy.
The 36-year-old vocal powerhouse—daughter of veteran Muzik Muzik host Datuk ND Lala—explained in a recent news report that heading to China was a "major sacrifice" made for the sake of her children.
"Leaving my children behind is painful, but it's necessary for my success," said Shila, whose real name is Nur Shahila Amir Amzah.
"I always tell myself to stay strong, because it is all for the good of my children and their future."
Shila shared that her seven-year-old son, Seth, often offers comforting words.
"He regularly tells me, 'Mama, you have to make your work easy and be happy,' which warms my heart," she said.
"To me, that means I shouldn't work to the point of exhaustion and should always enjoy what I do."
Praising her son for his maturity, she also apologised to Seth for celebrating his birthday a little late.
"His birthday fell on National Day (Aug 31), but I only celebrated it on Malaysia Day (Sept 16)," said Shila, who is set to leave for China soon.
"May my son grow into a successful and God-fearing young man. Seth, Mum and Dad love you so much. Mum hopes to make you proud through her hard work in China."
Seth is Shila's son from her first marriage to Haris Elias (2018–2022).
She also shares a two-year-old daughter, Rhea Akira, with her husband, influencer Muhammad Ubaidillah "Ubai" Zulkefli.
a728a75157f77685: SHAH ALAM: Mahkamah Tinggi hari ini menolak saman sivil RM1 juta difailkan seorang remaja perempuan yang menghidap 'cerebral palsy' bersama-sama ibu bapanya terhadap enam defendan, berhubung insiden dia terjatuh selepas seorang murid lain didakwa menarik kerusi ketika di sekolah pada 2023.
Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman Anita Harun turut memerintahkan pihak plaintif membayar kos RM10,000.

Menurut penghakiman, beliau memutuskan pihak plaintif gagal membuktikan kecuaian dan perkaitan sebab akibat yang diperlukan antara dakwaan kelemahan dalam penyeliaan serta penjagaan, dengan kecederaan atau penderitaan tambahan yang didakwa.

Mengenai dakwaan kecuaian penyeliaan, Anita berkata, defendan pertama mengakui beliau merupakan satu-satunya guru yang ada pada masa itu dan perhatiannya terbahagi antara dua kumpulan murid dengan keperluan yang berbeza.

Bagaimanapun, katanya, keterangan tidak membuktikan bahawa susunan penyeliaan itu tidak munasabah atau sebarang langkah berjaga-jaga munasabah yang telah diabaikan akan dapat mengelakkan kejatuhan tersebut.

“Plaintif pertama sendiri mengakui bahawa ia berlaku dengan pantas, tanpa didahului sebarang pertengkaran. Kecuaian penyeliaan, bahawa kejatuhan itu (disebabkan olehnya) tidak dapat dibuktikan,” katanya menambah, ketika kejadian, plaintif pertama sedang mengikuti Program Pendidikan Khas Integrasi (PPKI) di sebuah sekolah di Shah Alam.

Anita berkata, keputusan itu tidak menafikan kecederaan plaintif pertama atau beban yang ditanggung oleh keluarganya, tetapi ia mencerminkan kegagalan membuktikan kecuaian dan perkaitan sebab akibat yang diperlukan oleh undang-undang bagi mewujudkan liabiliti.

Terdahulu, Peguam Kanan Persekutuan Afiq Nazrin Zaharinan yang mewakili kesemua enam defendan memohon kos sebanyak RM30,000, manakala peguam plaintif, Sofian Azmir memohon RM10,000, sebelum pesuruhjaya kehakiman memerintahkan pihak plaintif membayar kos RM10,000 kepada kesemua enam defendan.

Saman itu difailkan bapa remaja terbabit, Wan Amey Shahril Wan Ab Rahman, 39, bagi pihak dirinya, isterinya dan anak perempuan mereka, terhadap enam defendan iaitu tiga orang guru Ilyana Sari Ridzuan, Suhaida Abdul Rahman dan Aizam Naim Mohd Junid; guru besar Hamidah Shamsudin; Kementerian Pendidikan Malaysia (KPM); dan kerajaan Malaysia.
Sementara itu, selepas prosiding, Sofian berkata, mereka tidak bersetuju dengan keputusan itu dan akan memfailkan rayuan tidak lama lagi.
“Kami tidak bersetuju dan kami percaya telah berlaku khilaf. Kami akan membuat rayuan secepat mungkin, atas sebab beberapa hujah tidak ditegaskan atau dinyatakan oleh Yang Arif.
“Kami mahu menegaskan bahawa kes ini membabitkan individu berkeperluan khas dan sepatutnya ada pemantauan,” katanya kepada media.

Pada Ogos 2024, media melaporkan bahawa remaja perempuan itu, yang ketika itu berusia 12 tahun, menderita selama hampir setahun akibat komplikasi daripada kecederaan tulang belakang, selepas beliau terjatuh apabila seorang rakan menarik kerusi yang baru hendak didudukinya.

Kejadian berlaku pada 12 Okt 2023 itu didedahkan oleh ibunya Azera Yazid, 38, di platform TikTok, sebelum keluarga tersebut mengambil tindakan undang-undang untuk menuntut pampasan atas kecederaan anak perempuan mereka dan kesan penderitaan yang dialaminya.
51aa717a000660fb: MOSCOW: Voting got underway on Friday in a three-day parliamentary election in Russia which president Vladimir Putin has framed as a barometer of support for Russia's war in Ukraine.

It is the first parliamentary election since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022, and the vote - which will determine the make-up of the 450-seat lower house of parliament, the State Duma - is widely expected to see the ruling pro-Putin United Russia party retain its dominance in what is a tightly controlled political system.

Most anti-war candidates have been excluded from the ballot after the Supreme Court ruled that the liberal Yabloko party - which wants a ceasefire - had breached electoral rules, though some Yabloko candidates are still running in individual constituencies.
In a televised address to the nation ahead of the vote, Putin said that casting a vote would help secure Russia's victory in Ukraine and demonstrate national resolve in the face of external pressure.
The Kremlin says national unity is vital because of what it says are increasingly dangerous efforts by Ukraine's intelligence services and other enemies to stir unrest inside Russia.
Voting is taking place at a time when opinion polls show some Russians have become more anxious about how the conflict affects them.

The economy is also under strain and the authorities are expected to use the vote to gauge the depth of society's war weariness as fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian drone strikes roil some parts of the country and businesses grapple with high interest rates, a labour crunch and Western sanctions.
Initial and partial results are expected to begin trickling out at 6pm on Sunday and near-complete results to be available on Monday.

e9de4aec7203b89b: KUALA LUMPUR: Pahang Umno will contribute to a fund set up to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay the RM50 million fine imposed under his conditional pardon.
Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the state chapter welcomed party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's initiative to launch the donation fund.
"Pahang Umno will also contribute to the fund as a sign of solidarity and support for the initiative announced by the Umno president," he said in a statement.
The state Umno liaison committee chairman also encouraged its members in Pahang who wished to contribute to do so voluntarily through their respective divisions.
He said all collections and contributions should be managed transparently and systematically, and in accordance with existing laws and regulations.
Earlier today, Zahid said Umno is launching a fundraising bid to help Najib pay the RM50 million fine.
He said this is meant to lighten Najib's burden in paying the fine.
Following that, Umno launched the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund.
Najib was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine.
The decision was made at the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya at Istana Negara today.

Under the conditional pardon, Najib must comply with the conditions imposed on him, failing which the pardon will be revoked and he will be required to return to prison to serve the remainder of his sentence.

1b148d81509320ad: PETALING JAYA: Police seized 191kg of drugs worth RM17.2 million in two separate raids in Kuching and Limbang over the past week.

Sarawak police chief Zainal Abdullah said the seizures involved various types of drugs, including MDMA powder and liquid, ketamine, Erimin 5 and methamphetamine. The raids also led to the arrest of two men aged 39 and 23.
Zainal said the seized drugs could have been distributed to about 484,850 people, highlighting the scale of the drug trafficking threat in Sarawak, reported Berita Harian.
In the first case in Kuching on Sept 11, police seized 107.518kg of drugs, comprising 50.1kg of MDMA powder, 32.3kg of ketamine, 25kg of liquid MDMA and 0.118kg of Erimin 5 pills.
“The total value of the seizure was estimated at RM12.89 million, with the drugs believed to have been intended for distribution in Kuching,” he said at a press conference in Kuching.
Following that, police raided a house at Jalan Mendamit in Limbang on Sept 14, where they seized 84.07kg of drugs comprising 81.21kg of methamphetamine, 2.06kg of ketamine and 0.80kg of MDMA powder.
The total value of the drugs seized was estimated at RM4.3 million. A four-wheel-drive vehicle worth RM35,000 was also seized.
Zainal said both cases were being investigated for drug trafficking under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
